rows: A match does not have to burn brightest at the start. Let the flame grow.
Brawling is a short line in a long story. Let me show you where the story goes.
A risk is a turn in the plot. I will take it, and you will feel it.
Slow is a long breath before the scene. I am happy to take one.
The people came to hear a story. Let me tell it well.
Plainly: this is a story, and it has a beginning, a middle and an end.
I am the one telling this story tonight, and I want to tell it carefully.
Read the stance like a line in a story. It is the first line of the scene.
Technique, you name it, as if it were a plot point. Show me the line in the story where it matters.
Strikes are the drama. The meaning is in what they change.
A risk in a story is only worth it if it changes the ending. Will yours?
A stall is a pause with nothing to say. I would rather tell the story.
The people deserve a story that is patient and earned. The crowd should have that.
You want a cheap reaction. I would rather give them a true one.
You are proud of your {strength}. It is a good line. Let me show you where it leads.
I have been reading your {strength} like a line in a book, and I know where the story turns.
You kept the scene steady. Fine. Calm is a line that changes meaning as the story goes on.
Fair. The scene allows it. That is a good line, and I will keep it in the story.
I could write a cruel line about that. I would rather write a true one.
One fall ends the chapter. The story closes on the count. Keep me down, and it will be your ending.
On the mat we are in the middle of the story. Read on with me.
Grounded or standing, the story keeps going.
Face me. This is the part where you show me what you are.
A passable line. It is the right line.
The next line is still blank. The story is waiting for the line.
Fair. The scene allows it. I will carry that line forward.
That line goes into the story. The ending is still to be written, and we will write it at the bell.
I will tell this match with patience, and I will let it end where it has to.
I tell this patiently. You will see the story on the night.
Whatever happens, the story will mean something.
The story is not over. The next line is still to come.
I have one more line, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
